Reply with JSON only: {"verdict":"PASS|FAIL","findings":[{"id":"F1","severity":"critical|high|medium|low","file":"...","line":0,"issue":"...","evidence":"quote the exact code","fix":"..."}],"confidence":0.0}. If you cannot quote the code that proves a finding, do not report it.

AUDIT QUESTION: Batch 75 = RULING 94 (orchestrator 2026-11-14 '00:40', to the builder, relayed verbatim): "94. Of the 23 Bitcoin Magazine interview moments, 13 never reach a judge because they open on a conjunction or a pronoun. For SPOTLIGHT and for a medley HOOK alike: (a) a leading conjunction or reply word gets ruling 33's ONE-word trim variant and that variant is what is rated as an opener (the trim must cut cleanly and the ALONE scorer must affirm it, as for a clip); (b) a first-person or second-person pronoun opener ('I', 'we', 'you', 'my', 'our') is NOT a cold-open fault at all: 'I will bet you one Bitcoin that...' is a fine first line; only a THIRD-person or demonstrative pronoun with no referent in the clip ('he', 'they', 'it', 'this', 'that') is, and the ALONE scorer + step A already judge exactly that. ... This touches the render's hook opener rule too: agree the change with the integrator, one audited change each side."
Context: pipeline/stand_alone.py is the render's (stage_validate's) opener / topic check, and the builder copies its bytes. (a) is already in check_edl: every segment whose lock trims a leading word (the hook included) is rated, and trimmed_opener requires the scorer to affirm; the trimmed hook's text starts after the trimmed word; an untrimmed hook opening on a conjunction or reply word stays a fault. Words come from canon.canon_tokens(heads=True) (a contraction reduces to its head: "we've" -> "we").
The change (agreed with the builder): FIRST_SECOND = {i, me, my, we, us, our, you, your}; THIRD = PRONOUNS - FIRST_SECOND (PRONOUNS unchanged). opener("hook"): a conjunction / reply word -> fault (unchanged); THIRD -> ok only with affirmed(score, fault, moments), no verdict -> fault (fail closed); FIRST_SECOND and anything else -> ok. check_edl's need (who the scorer rates) gains a hook opening on a THIRD word. Tests: test_stand_alone (must-fail / must-pass hooks per the ruling's examples; check_edl rates a THIRD hook and asks nobody for a first-person one; the auto-selection screen's hook example becomes a THIRD opener), test_trimmed_leading (a trimmed hook left opening on 'we' now opens; on 'they' it needs the scorer). 77 related tests pass; the 3 new ones fail on the old file.
FIND: a hook that opens on a third-person / demonstrative pronoun without an affirming verdict; a conjunction or reply-word hook that now opens untrimmed; a change to the CLIP opener rule; a word placed in the wrong set; a path where the scorer's verdict for the hook is not requested but read (fail open). Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

CODE:

diff --git a/pipeline/stand_alone.py b/pipeline/stand_alone.py

@@ -24,6 +24,11 @@ PRONOUNS = {"i", "me", "my", "it", "its", "this", "that", "these", "those", "the
 REPLY_FRAGMENTS = {"yeah", "yes", "yep", "no", "nope", "right", "exactly", "absolutely", "totally", "sure", "okay",
                    "ok", "oh", "well", "um", "uh", "agreed", "true", "correct", "indeed", "anyway", "anyways"}
 BACKREF = {"it", "its", "this", "that", "these", "those", "they"}
+# RULING 94 (b) (orchestrator 2026-11-14 '00:40'): a first- or second-person pronoun opener is NOT a cold-open fault
+# ("I will bet you one Bitcoin that..." is a fine first line); only a third-person or demonstrative pronoun with no
+# referent in the clip is, and the clip scorer judges exactly that (affirmed: it opens; else a fault, fail closed)
+FIRST_SECOND = {"i", "me", "my", "we", "us", "our", "you", "your"}
+THIRD = PRONOUNS - FIRST_SECOND
 BITCOIN = re.compile(r"\b(bitcoin|btc)\b", re.I)
 FIGURE = re.compile(r"\$\s?\d|\d\s?%|\bpercent\b|\b\d{1,3}(?:\s?,\s?\d{3})+\b|\b\d+(?:\s?\.\s?\d+)?\s?(?:k|thousand|million|billion)\b",
                     re.I)
@@ -78,9 +83,15 @@ def opener(kind, text, score=None, fault=None, moments=False):
         return False, "empty segment"
     w = ws[0]
     if kind == "hook":
-        for group, name in ((PRONOUNS, "pronoun"), (CONJUNCTIONS, "conjunction"), (REPLY_FRAGMENTS, "reply fragment")):
-            if w in group:
+        for group, name in ((CONJUNCTIONS, "conjunction"), (REPLY_FRAGMENTS, "reply fragment")):
+            if w in group:          # ruling 94 (a): only ruling 33's one-word trim variant opens (check_edl's trim rule)
                 return False, f"hook opens on the {name} {w!r}: nothing is heard before a hook"
+        if w in THIRD:              # ruling 94 (b): a referent the clip may not carry: the scorer judges it
+            if score is None:
+                return False, f"hook opens on the pronoun {w!r} and no clip-scorer verdict is available (fail closed)"
+            if affirmed(score, fault, moments):
+                return True, f"hook opens on {w!r}; the clip scorer affirms it stands alone ({score}, fault {fault})"
+            return False, f"hook opens on {w!r}; the clip scorer does not affirm it stands alone ({score}, fault {fault})"
         return True, f"opens on {w!r}"
     if w in CONJUNCTIONS or w in REPLY_FRAGMENTS:
         if score is None:
@@ -164,15 +175,17 @@ def trimmed_opener(word, score, fault, moments=False):
 
 def check_edl(edl, rate=None, subject=("bitcoin", "btc"), screen=None, moments=False):
     """Every segment of an EDL in order. rate(passages) -> {pid: (score, reason, fault)} is called only for
-    clips opening on a conjunction / reply fragment (the clip scorer) and for every segment whose lock trims a leading
-    word (ruling 33 part 2, the hook included); without it they fail closed.
+    clips opening on a conjunction / reply fragment (the clip scorer), for every segment whose lock trims a leading
+    word (ruling 33 part 2, the hook included) and for a hook opening on a third-person or demonstrative pronoun
+    (ruling 94 (b)); without it they fail closed.
     screen (ruling 34, a moments package's carried BTC_SCREEN, compiled): each segment's TOPIC test is the screen,
     and the medley must name Bitcoin (BITCOIN: bitcoin / btc) in at least one segment, the hook or a clip, in the
     speaker's own words. screen None: every segment names the subject, as before (the story path).
     moments (ruling 60, a moments pin): the scorer's verdict is read with affirmed(..., moments=True), the score alone."""
     segs = [("hook", "hook", edl["hook"])] + [(f"clip_{c['index']:02d}", "clip", c) for c in edl.get("clips", [])]
     need = [(label, s) for label, kind, s in segs if trimmed_word(s) or (kind == "clip" and _words(s.get("text"))[:1]
-            and (_words(s["text"])[0] in CONJUNCTIONS or _words(s["text"])[0] in REPLY_FRAGMENTS))]
+            and (_words(s["text"])[0] in CONJUNCTIONS or _words(s["text"])[0] in REPLY_FRAGMENTS))
+            or (kind == "hook" and _words(s.get("text"))[:1] and _words(s["text"])[0] in THIRD)]   # ruling 94 (b)
     scores, rate_error = {}, None
     if need and rate is not None:

     def test_hook_must_pass(self):
-        for text in (DATADASH, "Michael Saylor is back. Strategy purchased 1 ,036 Bitcoin."):
+        for text in (DATADASH, "Michael Saylor is back. Strategy purchased 1 ,036 Bitcoin.",

+                     "We've seen Bitcoin lose 16 %.", "I will bet you one Bitcoin that it holds.",  # second person is
+                     "You know, if you look at the chart, Bitcoin held.", "My view is simple: Bitcoin wins."):  # no fault
             self.assertTrue(S.opener("hook", text)[0], text)
+        ok, why = S.opener("hook", "This is ultimately a bipartisan issue.", 4.0, "none", moments=True)

+        first = {"hook": {"text": "I will bet you one Bitcoin that it holds.", "channel": "BM", "duration": 9.0},
+                 "clips": []}
+        asked.clear()
+        self.assertTrue(S.check_edl(first, rate=rate, moments=True)["rows"][0]["opener"]["pass"])
+        self.assertEqual(asked, [])                                  # a first-person hook asks nobody
 
     def test_clip_conjunction_needs_the_scorer(self):
